benchmark.category: a voice-ordered fireworks and effects Shot Kit builder with a live trending strip and a mock KHQR checkout for TikTok dancers
benchmark.users: TikTok dancers and small crews in Phnom Penh who plan, preview and order a 15-second fireworks shot from a phone

requirements.source_phrase: After trimming a kit to fit the budget, always keep 4 to 6 cues and always keep a firework on the drop second.
requirements.statement: POST /api/shot-kit returns a kit whose total_usd, recomputed from catalog prices, is at or below the budget stated in the request, cutting the cheapest non-drop lines first and keeping the drop line; the only exception is a budget too small for four cues plus the drop firework, where the 4-6 cue rule wins and the total may exceed the budget by at most the cheapest accepted cue.
requirements.notes: The user's later line makes the cue minimum and the drop firework outrank the budget; the build reports budgets under $4 may go slightly over. Test $5, $10, $25, '80,000 riel' and $2.

requirements.source_phrase: If the kit LLM call fails or returns invalid JSON, retry once, then fall back to a valid kit built from the catalog within budget.
requirements.statement: POST /api/shot-kit retries the LLM exactly once when the call errors or its output fails the kit contract (non-JSON, wrong field set, out-of-range cue second, non-catalog item, totals that do not recompute from the cart), and if the retry also fails it responds 200 with the valid catalog fallback kit instead of the invalid output or an error status.
requirements.notes: Reverses the inherited reject-with-error rule; count provider attempts (two, not one and not three) and assert the 200 body is a complete valid kit.

requirements.source_phrase: The user must never see "Could not build your Shot Kit".
requirements.statement: When a kit request gets no usable response from the server at all (network failure or 5xx), the card area shows a short English message naming the problem, the Build control re-enables, and any previous kit stays clearly labelled or is cleared; the text 'Could not build your Shot Kit' never appears for any path.
requirements.notes: The AI-failure half of the old requirement is replaced by the fallback kit; what remains is the genuine transport-failure path and the non-stale-card rule.

requirements.source_phrase: After trimming a kit to fit the budget, always keep 4 to 6 cues and always keep a firework on the drop second.
requirements.statement: When the stated budget cannot cover four cues plus the drop firework (for example a budget under $4), POST /api/shot-kit still returns a valid kit with 4 to 6 cues and a firework at drop_second whose total_usd may exceed the budget by at most the cheapest accepted cue, instead of a 'no kit fits' error or an empty cart.
requirements.notes: Replaces the below-minimum refusal: the 4-6 cue and drop-firework rules now outrank the budget boundary.

requirements.source_phrase: Under the tagline add: "Tell us your dance. We build the fireworks for your 15 second shot and deliver by tuk-tuk in Phnom Penh."
requirements.statement: Under the tagline on / the intro line 'Tell us your dance. We build the fireworks for your 15 second shot and deliver by tuk-tuk in Phnom Penh.' renders as visible body copy, complete and unclipped at 390px and at 1280px wide.
requirements.notes: Copy is user-given character for character; check the rendered string including the final period and the hyphen in 'tuk-tuk'.

requirements.source_phrase: Next to the text input add the hint "Tip: dictate your order with Willow".
requirements.statement: Next to the text input on / the screen shows the hint 'Tip: dictate your order with Willow', visible without opening a menu or scrolling past the input.
requirements.notes: Exact copy from the user's line; a paraphrase is a mismatch.

requirements.source_phrase: Add the footer "Built by voice with Willow. Live trends by You.com. Shipped on Emergent."
requirements.statement: The bottom of / shows the footer 'Built by voice with Willow. Live trends by You.com. Shipped on Emergent.', reachable by scrolling at 390px wide and rendered in full on one or more lines.
requirements.notes: Exact copy; the footer must not be hidden behind the order dialog or clipped by the page bottom.

requirements.source_phrase: Add a "Trending tonight" strip above the mic.
requirements.statement: On load / shows a 'Trending tonight' strip above the mic button, populated from GET /api/trends, with a loading state that resolves into the chips (or the fallback chips) rather than a blank bar or an endless spinner.
requirements.notes: The build's test list names data-testid trending-strip; position is above the mic, not below the kit card.

requirements.source_phrase: Show them as tappable chips that add to the request.
requirements.statement: Each returned trend renders as a chip showing the song's title and artist or the event's name and place, and tapping a chip adds that song or event text into the request input so the next build request carries it.
requirements.notes: Build test list names trend-chip-N and expects tapping to append into manual-text-input; the appended text must be readable in the input, not only in state.

requirements.source_phrase: On load, the backend calls GET https://ydc-index.io/v1/search with header X-API-Key, for "trending TikTok dance songs this week" and "Phnom Penh events tonight".
requirements.statement: GET /api/trends makes real HTTPS requests to https://ydc-index.io/v1/search with the key in an X-API-Key header, one search for 'trending TikTok dance songs this week' and one for 'Phnom Penh events tonight', and returns JSON holding up to 4 sounds (title, artist) and up to 2 events (name, place) extracted from those results.
requirements.notes: Word it as a real outbound request through the app's own code path: assert host, path, header name, both query strings and the response shape. The build report itself notes an odd live pick, so check shape and provenance rather than taste.

requirements.statement: Every returned sound carries non-empty title and artist strings and every returned event non-empty name and place strings, the lists never exceed 4 sounds or 2 events, no entry is empty or duplicated, and each entry can be traced to a result in the You.com response rather than being invented.
requirements.notes: AI class content check against a recorded or stubbed You.com payload; the user's line names the fields (title, artist) and (name, place), so a missing artist or an invented event is a failure.

requirements.source_phrase: Cache results for 10 minutes.
requirements.statement: Two GET /api/trends calls made within 10 minutes produce one outbound You.com search and the same payload, and a call after the cache expires issues a fresh search and may return new picks.
requirements.notes: Count outbound provider requests via stub or log; the 10-minute window is user-given.

requirements.source_phrase: If the call fails or takes over 4 seconds, use a hardcoded fallback of 3 sounds and 1 event.
requirements.statement: When the You.com search errors, returns unusable content or takes longer than 4 seconds, GET /api/trends still answers 200 within about 4 seconds with exactly the hardcoded fallback of 3 sounds and 1 event, each carrying title+artist or name+place.
requirements.notes: Simulate a 500 and a 5-second provider delay and measure the endpoint's own response time. The label shown for these chips is the build's choice; the count and shape are the user's.

requirements.source_phrase: On the Shot Kit card add a "Why this kit" section listing 2 to 3 source titles with links, labeled "Built from live search, powered by You.com".
requirements.statement: Each Shot Kit card shows a 'Why this kit' section with 2 to 3 source titles, each title a working link to its http(s) source URL, and the section labelled 'Built from live search, powered by You.com'.
requirements.notes: Build test list names why-this-kit, why-source-link-N and you-com-label; count the links (2 or 3, never 0 or 4) and read the label text exactly.

requirements.source_phrase: On the Shot Kit card add a "Why this kit" section listing 2 to 3 source titles with links, labeled "Built from live search, powered by You.com".
requirements.statement: The kit JSON from POST /api/shot-kit carries 2 to 3 sources, each with a non-empty title and a unique http(s) url drawn from the trending search results or the hardcoded fallback set, and no URL the language model invented is passed through.
requirements.notes: Content check: URLs must be http(s), unique and members of the set GET /api/trends returns (or the fallback), since the label promises live-search provenance.

requirements.source_phrase: If the kit LLM call fails or returns invalid JSON, retry once, then fall back to a valid kit built from the catalog within budget.
requirements.statement: POST /api/shot-kit calls the LLM once, retries exactly once when the call errors or the output fails the kit contract, and if the retry also fails returns 200 with a catalog-built kit that satisfies the full contract (4-6 cues with one at drop_second, catalog-only item_ids, totals recomputed from catalog prices within the stated budget, total_khr = total_usd x 4000, 2-3 sources) instead of an error body.
requirements.notes: Force failure with an invalid LLM key or a stub returning malformed JSON; assert exactly two provider attempts and a valid 200 kit. The hard part is that the fallback must itself be valid, not merely present.

requirements.source_phrase: The user must never see "Could not build your Shot Kit".
requirements.statement: No state of / renders the text 'Could not build your Shot Kit' — when the AI call fails the card shows the catalog fallback kit — and the phrase appears nowhere in the page DOM or the served JS bundle.
requirements.notes: Drive a build with a broken AI key so the failure path is exercised, then also grep the built assets for the phrase to catch a dormant conditional message.

requirements.source_phrase: After trimming a kit to fit the budget, always keep 4 to 6 cues and always keep a firework on the drop second.
requirements.statement: After any budget trim the returned kit has 4 to 6 cues, exactly one cue at drop_second, and that drop cue's catalog item still present in the cart with qty of at least 1, for both the LLM-produced kit and the fallback kit.
requirements.notes: The build admits budgets under $4 may go slightly over budget: record that the 4-cue minimum and the drop firework take priority over the budget in that case.

requirements.source_phrase: Store it in backend .env as YDC_API_KEY.
requirements.statement: The backend reads the You.com key from backend/.env under the name YDC_API_KEY at startup and uses it only in the server-side X-API-Key request header, with no key literal in source and no key committed to the repository.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class; required_credentials says 'None (YDC_API_KEY and EMERGENT_LLM_KEY set in environment)'.

requirements.source_phrase: Never expose it in frontend code.
requirements.statement: The YDC_API_KEY value appears in no API response body, page source, JS bundle, browser network request or server log line, and the browser never calls ydc-index.io directly.
requirements.notes: Search the served bundle and all API responses for the key string; a proxied endpoint that echoes the request headers is the usual leak.

requirements.source_phrase: Include these results in the kit LLM prompt.
requirements.statement: The prompt POST /api/shot-kit sends to the model contains the trending sounds and events the app holds (the cached live set, or the hardcoded fallback when search failed), and building a kit still succeeds when that list is empty.
requirements.notes: Inspect the captured outbound LLM payload; also confirm an empty trends list does not break prompt construction.

requirements.source_phrase: Add an "Order this kit" button.
requirements.statement: A built Shot Kit card shows an 'Order this kit' button that opens the order dialog, and no Order button is offered before a kit has been built.
requirements.notes: Build test list names order-kit-button and the order-dialog it opens.

requirements.source_phrase: It asks for a delivery spot from a list of Phnom Penh landmarks (Riverside, Koh Pich, Wat Phnom, Independence Monument, Night Market) and a time
requirements.statement: The order dialog offers exactly the five landmarks Riverside, Koh Pich, Wat Phnom, Independence Monument and Night Market plus a delivery-time input, marks the chosen landmark as selected, and keeps the continue action disabled until both a landmark and a time are set.
requirements.notes: Build test list names order-spot-koh-pich, order-time-input and order-continue-btn; the list must offer all five values, not a shortened set.

requirements.source_phrase: then shows a mock KHQR payment code
requirements.statement: After continuing, the order dialog shows a KHQR payment card containing a mock, non-scannable payment code, the amount in riel and a note that the payment is a mock, and no real payment credential or card field is requested.
requirements.notes: Build test list names khqr-card, khqr-amount-khr, mock-khqr-code and mock-payment-note. The app note states the payment is intentionally mocked, so the check is that no real charge path exists.

requirements.source_phrase: then a confirmation screen with an order number and status steps (Packed, On the tuk-tuk, Arrived).
requirements.statement: Confirming the mock payment shows a confirmation screen carrying an order number in the form BD-XXXXXX and three named status steps: Packed, On the tuk-tuk and Arrived.
requirements.notes: Build test list names order-confirmation, order-number and order-status-steps; the order number must be the stored one, not a fresh client-side random per render.

requirements.source_phrase: Read the confirmation aloud with browser speech synthesis.
requirements.statement: The confirmation screen has a read-aloud control that speaks the confirmation through the browser's speechSynthesis API with an utterance naming the order number and at least one status step, while the same text stays readable on screen.
requirements.notes: Headless browsers cannot be listened to: stub speechSynthesis and assert speak() is called with a non-empty string containing the order number; the app note confirms audio cannot be heard in the preview environment.

requirements.statement: Completing checkout writes one order row holding the order number, the chosen landmark, the delivery time, the kit's line items, total_usd and total_khr, and reading that order back by its number after a repeat request or a server restart returns the same values.
requirements.notes: From the build description 'Orders are saved in the database.' The user's own line stops at the confirmation screen, so persistence is derived from the build account; a confirmation built purely from client state would still satisfy the user's words but fail this.

requirements.source_phrase: Add an "Order this kit" button.
requirements.statement: POST /api/orders takes the kit payload, one of the five landmarks and a delivery time, stores exactly one order with a unique BD-XXXXXX number and the kit's line items and totals, and returns the stored order; a missing kit, a missing landmark, a landmark outside the five or a missing time is refused with a 4xx and stores nothing.
requirements.notes: Enforce the dialog's rules on the server as well as the screen; a direct POST with a made-up landmark must be refused.

requirements.source_phrase: tap a trending chip, build a kit, play the 3D preview, order the kit, reach the confirmation
requirements.statement: In one session at a 390x844 viewport a user can tap a trending chip, build a kit, open and close the 3D preview, choose a landmark and time, pass the mock KHQR screen and reach the confirmation with its order number, with no dead end, blank step or uncaught console error along the way.
requirements.notes: This is the end-to-end promise of the request; the individual steps are covered separately, but a step that only works in isolation fails here.

requirements.source_phrase: Keep all existing features and design.
requirements.statement: With the trending strip, Why this kit and checkout added, / still records and transcribes voice input, builds kits from typed text, shows the catalog, opens the 3D preview with Stage/Phone toggle and the 2D fallback, and needs no login — the pre-existing flows behave as before.
requirements.notes: Regression guard for this pass; distinct from R-091, which guards the preview pass. Re-run one typed build and one preview open after the new features land.

requirements.source_phrase: Do not change the design.
requirements.statement: The screens added in this pass keep the existing BoomDrop design: the tagline 'Fireworks that hit on the drop.', the dark night-sky background and the neon pink and gold accents still render, and no existing screen is restyled or replaced.
requirements.notes: The subjective part of 'do not change the design' is unmeasurable; test only that the named tagline and theme from R-001 survive on the new screens.

requirements.statement: Tapping a trend chip appends its text to the request input once and marks that chip selected while it is selected, and tapping the same chip again does not append a duplicate copy of the text.
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of 'tappable chips that add to the request': the control must change its own state and act once.

requirements.statement: After tapping the chip for a trending song and building, the returned kit's song field names that song (or the kit text visibly references it), so a chip tap demonstrably changes the kit rather than being decorative.
requirements.notes: Derived from 'tapping a chip adds it to the request' plus 'Include these results in the kit LLM prompt'; keeps the trending strip from being a display-only ornament.

requirements.statement: When the trends payload holds no chips, the strip either hides itself or shows a one-line 'No trends right now' message, never an empty bordered bar or a spinner that never resolves.
requirements.notes: Zero-row state of a shown list; the backend fallback should make it unreachable, which is why reaching it is itself a finding.

requirements.statement: When GET /api/trends fails at the network level the strip still renders the hardcoded fallback chips and the mic, text box and Build control remain usable, with no provider error text shown to the user.
requirements.notes: Failure half of the strip: a failed fetch must not block ordering or empty the page.

requirements.statement: While the trends request is still running the user can type, record and press Build, and a trends response arriving later never overwrites text already in the request input or a kit already on the card.
requirements.notes: The build note says the first call can take 5-15s; a late response that clobbers user input is the failure this catches.

requirements.statement: When the trending search yields fewer than 2 usable sources the kit still returns 2 to 3 source entries padded from the hardcoded fallback set, never one entry and never an empty 'Why this kit' section.
requirements.notes: Boundary of the 2-3 rule; test with a stubbed single-result search.

requirements.statement: Each 'Why this kit' source link opens its https URL in a new tab without navigating the app away from the kit, and each link's visible title is a real string rather than 'undefined' or an empty anchor.
requirements.notes: Control-exists-half: the link must actually go somewhere and must not destroy the built kit.

requirements.statement: The fallback kit returned when both LLM attempts fail carries the same field set as a normal kit (kit_name, song under 6 words with no parentheses, 4-6 cues inside 0-15s with one at drop_second, catalog-only cart, recomputed totals, 2-3 sources), so every card section renders from it.
requirements.notes: The user asks for 'a valid kit built from the catalog within budget'; a fallback that omits cues, sources or totals would still leave parts of the card blank.

requirements.statement: The KHQR card's amount in riel equals the ordered kit's total_khr for that kit, and the confirmation repeats the same amount and the same USD total, both to whole riel.
requirements.notes: A displayed value must equal the stored value it is labelled as; a client-side recomputation at a different rate would show here.

requirements.statement: Closing the order dialog before confirming, by its close control or Escape, returns to the Shot Kit card with the same kit and totals and leaves no order row and no charge behind.
requirements.notes: Inverse of 'Add an Order this kit button'; a dialog that traps the user or half-writes an order is the defect.

requirements.statement: The mock-payment confirm control advances to the confirmation once; a double tap or a repeated click produces exactly one order and one confirmation, not two order numbers.
requirements.notes: One payment intent, one order; the mock path most often forgets this because there is no provider to enforce it.

requirements.statement: A delivery time that has already passed is refused in the order dialog with a readable message while a future time is accepted, so the user cannot order delivery for a moment that is already gone.
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of 'and a time': assumption recorded in notes is that Phnom Penh same-day delivery cannot be scheduled in the past; if the product later allows pre-dating an order, this becomes conditional.

requirements.statement: When browser speech synthesis is unavailable or refuses to start, the confirmation still shows its full text and says speech is unavailable, and the read-aloud control never claims it is speaking when no utterance started.
requirements.notes: Failure path the build's own open items flag ('if sound can't start, the mute button still shows sound as on'); nothing may fail silently.

requirements.statement: After the mock payment is confirmed the dialog shows a visible working state until the confirmation appears, so a slow status transition never looks like a dead button.
requirements.notes: Nothing succeeds silently; the build's status steps advance on a timer, so the gap before the first step is the vulnerable window.

requirements.statement: The order stored at checkout carries the same line items, total_usd and total_khr as the kit that was ordered, and the confirmation's amount equals those stored totals rather than a value recomputed in the browser.
requirements.notes: Business-logic class: a value changed in one place must change everywhere it is shown; compare the stored order against the kit payload.

requirements.statement: The intro line, the Willow hint, the footer and the chip labels meet at least 4.5:1 contrast against their backgrounds in the dark theme, measured on the rendered colours.
requirements.notes: Layout/UX class; small footer and hint text on a dark neon theme is where contrast normally fails.

requirements.source_phrase: Test on a mobile viewport too.
requirements.statement: At 390x844 the intro line, the Willow hint, the footer and the trending strip render without page-level horizontal overflow, with the chip row scrolling horizontally inside its own container.
requirements.notes: Build test list names 390x844 and 'no horizontal overflow outside the scroll chips'.

requirements.source_phrase: Test on a mobile viewport too.
requirements.statement: At 390x844 the order dialog fits the viewport, all five landmarks are reachable by scrolling inside the dialog, and the time input and continue control stay visible without clipping or overlapping.
requirements.notes: Build test list says 'dialog fits'; a bottom sheet taller than the viewport with the continue button off-screen is the common defect.

requirements.source_phrase: Test on a mobile viewport too.
requirements.statement: At 390x844 the confirmation shows the order number and all three status steps without horizontal scrolling, and the read-aloud control is reachable.
requirements.notes: Mobile viewport promise for the new terminal screen.

requirements.statement: The three status steps advance in order Packed to On the tuk-tuk to Arrived on a timer of a few seconds each, mark exactly one step as current at a time, reach Arrived and never move backwards.
requirements.notes: Build test list expects the steps to advance over about 9 seconds; the app note says the steps are simulated on a timer.

requirements.statement: The stored order's status moves Packed to On the tuk-tuk to Arrived in that order and is readable by order number, ending at Arrived and never regressing to an earlier step.
requirements.notes: State transitions the domain allows; whether the timer runs on the server or the client, the stored order must reach Arrived.

requirements.statement: The utterance handed to speech synthesis is a non-empty confirmation sentence naming the order number and at least one status step, not the raw URL, a placeholder or an empty string.
requirements.notes: Content check of generated speech rather than a status check: stub speechSynthesis and inspect the spoken string.

requirements.statement: The mock payment step makes no request to any payment provider and needs no payment key; it marks the stored order as mock-paid and returns the same amount the kit's total_khr carries.
requirements.notes: Payments class against a deliberately mocked flow: the requirement is that no real charge path exists and the amount shown matches the kit.

requirements.statement: Replaying the mock-payment confirmation request for one checkout attempt produces exactly one stored order and one status timeline, never a duplicate order row.
requirements.notes: Idempotency of the payment confirmation, which the mock path must simulate since no provider dedupes it.

requirements.statement: A 429 or 5xx from You.com is handled like any other failure: the cached set is served if fresh, otherwise the hardcoded fallback is served with 200, and no provider error string or status reaches the browser.
requirements.notes: Third-party class: an external provider's error must not become the app's error page.

requirements.statement: With YDC_API_KEY absent from the environment the app still boots, GET /api/trends returns the hardcoded fallback with 200, and POST /api/shot-kit still builds kits.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class: no setting read that the environment may lack should crash a route.

requirements.statement: GET / serves the page with every script, style and image the trending strip, Why this kit and checkout components reference returning 200 and no uncaught console error on first paint.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class for the newly added surfaces.

requirements.statement: Opening, closing and reopening the order dialog several times and leaving the confirmation page leaves one live status timer and one speech utterance at a time, so no step fires twice and no queued speech plays over a later order.
requirements.notes: Resource-leak class: interval and speechSynthesis queues stacked across dialog opens are the usual defect.

requirements.statement: The order dialog prefills the landmark and delivery time the user chose on their previous order, so a repeat order needs only a confirmation rather than re-picking both.
requirements.notes: benchmark: delivery checkouts remember the last address and time; a tuk-tuk delivery user in Phnom Penh orders repeatedly from the same spot, and re-entering both every time is the friction they notice.

requirements.statement: Before the mock payment card the order dialog shows the kit's total in USD and riel together with the chosen landmark and time, so the user sees what they are about to pay before reaching the KHQR screen.
requirements.notes: benchmark: every checkout shows the amount on the review step, not only on the payment screen; users judge a delivery flow by seeing the bill before paying.

retired.reason: the user's line 'After trimming a kit to fit the budget, always keep 4 to 6 cues and always keep a firework on the drop second.' removes the over-budget-error-and-no-kit path R-071 required; the amended R-032 now covers that boundary as a slightly-over-budget kit
retired.summary: When cutting non-drop lines cannot bring the kit within budget, POST /api/shot-kit returns an explicit over-budget error and no kit, never a kit above the budget and never an empty cart carrying a total.

retired.reason: the user's line 'If the kit LLM call fails or returns invalid JSON, retry once, then fall back to a valid kit built from the catalog within budget. The user must never see "Could not build your Shot Kit".' replaces the visible error for a missing or invalid key with a catalog fallback kit; the transcription error path stays covered by R-059 and R-028
retired.summary: With EMERGENT_LLM_KEY absent or invalid, POST /api/shot-kit and POST /api/transcribe return a visible error the screen shows, never an empty string, a canned kit or an apology card
